images.title: Same size pieces, more pieces
images.purpose: Show two chocolate bars of the same size, each cut into 10 equal pieces, with 3 pieces shaded on one and 7 on the other, so the bar with more pieces of the same size is clearly the greater fraction.
images.composition: Two long bars of equal length one above the other, the person's name above each, its fraction at the right, and the comparison written large across the bottom.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two horizontal bars, one above the other, exactly the same size: each bar is 1000 px wide and 110 px high with its left edge at x 150, a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px) and exactly 9 thin dark cut lines (2 px) that divide it into exactly 10 equal pieces, each piece 100 px wide and 110 px high. TOP BAR (top edge at y 200): the first 3 pieces from the left filled teal #0072B2 and the other 7 pieces white. BOTTOM BAR (top edge at y 430): the first 7 pieces from the left filled amber #E69F00 and the other 3 pieces white. Above the left end of the top bar the name Tamanna and above the left end of the bottom bar the name Gurpreet, both in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (40 px). At the right of each bar, level with the middle of the bar and starting about 30 px after its right edge, its fraction in dark bold numerals (72 px): 3/10 beside the top bar and 7/10 beside the bottom bar. Across the bottom centre, about y 690, one line of bold dark text, 7/10 > 3/10 (80 px), the largest text in the frame. In all 20 pieces, of which 10 are shaded (3 teal, 7 amber). Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
bars of different lengths or heights, or pieces of unequal width
any piece shaded other than the first 3 of the top bar and the first 7 of the bottom bar
images.takeaway: With pieces of the same size, 7 pieces of 1/10 are more than 3 pieces of 1/10, so 7/10 > 3/10.
images.description: Two bars of the same size, each cut into 10 equal pieces, with 3 pieces shaded on Tamanna's bar and 7 on Gurpreet's bar, and 7/10 > 3/10 written below.
images.context: Concept image for More Pieces of the Same Size (comparing with the same denominator). It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (one whole cut into equal pieces with some pieces marked) and shows the concept's own example, 3/10 and 7/10 of two chocolate bars of the same size.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the child to count the pieces on each bar first (10 and 10, so the pieces are the same size) and only then the shaded ones. The slip to watch is the thought that a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction: here the bottom numbers are equal and only the count of pieces differs.

image_decisions.why: Two bars of the same size cut into 10 equal pieces, with 3 and 7 pieces shaded, make the idea of same-size pieces and the count that decides visible.
